```{r sourceData, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tigris)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)

library(ggrepel)


# get the most updated data files
source("data_preprocessing/mass_processing.R")
# set working directory -- I have to do this after sourcing the data because it loses the path otherwise
setwd("C:\\Users\\ar2529\\Desktop\\overdose_age")
source("data_preprocessing/ocme_processing.R")
setwd("C:\\Users\\ar2529\\Desktop\\overdose_age")

```

```{r importData, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# import ct data 

ocme_2018 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2018_processed.csv")
ocme_2019 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2019_processed.csv")
ocme_2020 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2020_processed.csv")
ocme_2021 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2021_processed.csv")
ocme_2022 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2022_processed.csv")
ocme_2023 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2023_processed.csv")

# import 2009-2017 ct data 

ocme_old <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/ocme_2009_2017_processed.csv")

# split the dataset by year [so we can use it to split into old/young age], from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57454085/assign-a-variable-in-r-using-another-variable

for(i in unique(ocme_old$Year)){
  assign(paste0("ocme_", as.character(i)), subset(ocme_old, Year == as.character(i)))
}

# import mass data 

mass_2018 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_2018_processed.csv")
mass_2019 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_2019_processed.csv")
mass_2020 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_2020_processed.csv")
mass_2021 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_2021_processed.csv")
mass_2022 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_2022_processed.csv")
mass_2023 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_2023_processed.csv")

# import 2009-2017 mass data 

mass_old <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/mass_old_processed.csv")

# split the dataset by year [so we can use it to split into old/young age], from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57454085/assign-a-variable-in-r-using-another-variable

for(i in unique(mass_old$Year)){
  assign(paste0("mass_", as.character(i)), subset(mass_old, Year == as.character(i)))
}

```

### Age distribution for all MA fatal and nonfatal overdoses {.tabset}

#### 2009

```{r age2009MA, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
# looks like there are some NAs in the 2009 data so I have to get rid of them
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(na.omit(mass_2009$age)) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(mass_2009$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(mass_2009$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
mass_2009_young <- subset(mass_2009, age <= antimodes[1])
mass_2009_old <- subset(mass_2009, age > antimodes[1])

# create a condition to use different colors based on the location of the antimode
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13372523/altering-the-color-of-one-value-in-a-ggplot-histogram
# it just gives me a 0 for anything in the younger population, 1 for older

mass_2009$aftermode <- mass_2009$age > antimodes[1]

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=mass_2009, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = mass_2009$age, labels = mass_2009$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2009 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2009 <- ggplot(data=mass_2009, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = mass_2009$age, labels = mass_2009$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2009 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2009

ggsave(plot=age_2009, filename = "images/mass/age_2009.png", width = 10, height = 8)


sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(mass_2009$age)$p.value) 

```

#### 2015


```{r age2015MA, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
# looks like there are some NAs in the 2015 data so I have to get rid of them
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(na.omit(mass_2015$age)) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(mass_2015$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(mass_2015$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode

# THIS IS A UNIMODAL DISTRIBUTION! NOT INCLUDING? 
mass_2015_young <- subset(mass_2015, age <= antimodes[1])
mass_2015_old <- subset(mass_2015, age > antimodes[1])


# create a condition to use different colors based on the location of the antimode
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13372523/altering-the-color-of-one-value-in-a-ggplot-histogram
# it just gives me a 0 for anything in the younger population, 1 for older

mass_2015$aftermode <- mass_2015$age > antimodes[1]


#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=mass_2015, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = mass_2015$age, labels = mass_2015$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2015 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2015 <- ggplot(data=mass_2015, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = mass_2015$age, labels = mass_2015$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2015 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2015

ggsave(plot=age_2015, filename = "images/mass/age_2015.png", width = 10, height = 8)


sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(mass_2015$age)$p.value) 

 
```

#### 2022

```{r age2022MA, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(mass_2022$age) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(mass_2022$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(mass_2022$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
# in this case we have to use the second antimode because the first one seems to represent some infant deaths
mass_2022_young <- subset(mass_2022, age <= antimodes[1])
mass_2022_old <- subset(mass_2022, age > antimodes[1])

# create a condition to use different colors based on the location of the antimode
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13372523/altering-the-color-of-one-value-in-a-ggplot-histogram
# it just gives me a 0 for anything in the younger population, 1 for older

mass_2022$aftermode <- mass_2022$age > antimodes[1]

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=mass_2022, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = aftermode), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = mass_2022$age, labels = mass_2022$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2022 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")


# using modes[-1] to get rid of that first mode which is for a baby death
age_2022 <- ggplot(data=mass_2022, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = aftermode), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = mass_2022$age, labels = mass_2022$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1, color="black") + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2022 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2022


ggsave(plot=age_2022, filename = "images/mass/age_2022.png", width = 10, height = 8)

sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(mass_2022$age)$p.value) 

```

### Significance testing for sex

#### CT

```{r chiSquaredSexOCME, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_sex <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "p value")

for(i in 1:length(ocmelistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- ocmelistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- ocmelistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  sexfreqtable <- young %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
  names(sexfreqtable)[names(sexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  sextableold <- old %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
  names(sextableold)[names(sextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  sextable <- merge(sexfreqtable, sextableold, by="Sex_revised")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  sexmat <- sextable[,-1]
  rownames(sexmat) <- sextable[,1]

  print(as.matrix(sexmat))
  
  # append year and p value to a vector, rounding to make it more legible
  # I'm using Fisher's exact test if >20% of cell counts are <5, if not use chi squared
  # I get >20% <5 from https://www.ccjm.org/content/84/9_suppl_2/e20
  pvalue <- ifelse(sum(sexmat < 5)/(ncol(sexmat) * nrow(sexmat)) > 0.2, round(fisher.test(as.matrix(sexmat))$p.value, 4), round(chisq.test(as.matrix(sexmat))$p.value, 4))
  
  results <- c(year, pvalue)
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_sex <- rbind(chisq_sex, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_sex) <- cols

chisq_sex

```

```{r chiSquaredWhiteCT, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  # the year column in 2018 is "year" instead of "Year" which is causing the issue
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  racefreqtable <- subset(young, race_numeric_words == "White") %>% group_by(race_numeric_words) %>% tally()
  names(racefreqtable)[names(racefreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  racetableold <- subset(old, race_numeric_words == "White") %>% group_by(race_numeric_words) %>% tally()
  names(racetableold)[names(racetableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  racetable <- merge(racefreqtable, racetableold, by="race_numeric_words")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  racemat <- racetable[,-1]
  
  # add to matrix with all the white results 
  
  results <- cbind(year, racemat)
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_white <- rbind(chisq_white, results)

}
```

```{r raceLatine, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# change the col names to be more informative
names(propRace) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# create grouped bar plot, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72449952/making-a-grouped-bar-chart-in-r
# getting the labels in the right position from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37587288/ggplot-label-bars-in-grouped-bar-plot
# info on changing legend title from here https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41649929/how-to-modify-a-legend-title-in-a-barplot-with-ggplot
# the scale x continuous is there because for some reason adding 2023 data messed up the x axis, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72051789/how-to-display-all-values-on-x-and-y-axes-in-r-ggplot2

# increasing line size from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14794599/how-to-change-line-width-in-ggplot
# line graph info from https://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-line-plot-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization

pracelong  <- propRace |>
  # Reshape data to long format
  pivot_longer(Younger:Older)

# create labels with the value of each proportion
pracelong$labels <- round(pracelong$value, 2)

pRace <-  ggplot(data = pracelong, aes(x = Year, y = value, fill = name, group=name, color=factor(name))) +
  # Implement a grouped bar chart
  # Implement a line graph
  geom_line(stat = "identity", size = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Proportion of Latine opioid-detected overdose deaths \n by age group in MA, 2009-2023") + ylab("Proportion") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + scale_fill_discrete(guide="none") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=propRace$Year) + xlab("Year")+ coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) + guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Age group"))+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = labels, x = Year, y = value), nudge_x = 0.1, na.rm = FALSE, color = "black", size = 2.5, label.size = NA, fill = NA)

pRace

ggsave(plot=pRace, filename = "images/mass/prop_latine_allyears.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

#### Significance testing for Latine deaths

**CT**

```{r chiSquaredLatineCT, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_latine <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

for(i in 1:length(ocmelistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- ocmelistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- ocmelistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  racefreqtable <- subset(young, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic") %>% group_by(race_numeric_words) %>% tally()
  names(racefreqtable)[names(racefreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  racetableold <- subset(old, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic") %>% group_by(race_numeric_words) %>% tally()
  names(racetableold)[names(racetableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  racetable <- merge(racefreqtable, racetableold, by="race_numeric_words")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  racemat <- racetable[,-1]
  
  # add to matrix with all the white results 
  
  results <- cbind(year, racemat)
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_latine <- rbind(chisq_latine, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_latine) <- cols

chisq_latine

# compute chi squared

racemat <- as.matrix(chisq_latine[,-1])

  pvalue <- ifelse(sum(racemat < 5)/(ncol(racemat) * nrow(racemat)) > 0.2, round(fisher.test(as.matrix(racemat))$p.value, 4), round(chisq.test(as.matrix(racemat))$p.value, 4))

pvalue

```

### Race/sex of decedents

**Young**

```{r racesexYoung, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# create dummy df with race sex info for all years

racesexmat <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "Race_sex", "Proportion", "Color")

for(i in 1:length(ocmelistYoung)){

  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  ocme <- ocmelistYoung[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- ocme$Year[1]

  # remove any not listed as male/female because having 1-2 people in one year isn't informative/doesn't show up properly on a     graph that tracks changes over time
  # info on trans people available in the pie charts!
  
  ocme <- subset(ocme, Sex_revised %in% c("Male", "Female"))
  

# get the % of each race sex category
ocme <- ocme %>% 
  group_by(race_sex) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(per=`n`/sum(`n`)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(race_sex))
# create a label out of this
ocme$racesexlabel <- scales::percent(ocme$per)


# create a year label [for plotting]
ocme$Year <- year

# automatically assign the color based on race sex value -- not doing this in preprocessing because I don't want this to be a global change
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39142596/r-ggplot-set-colour-for-specific-value

ocme$color <- ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "Black Female", "#e6d0a1", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "Black Male", "#E69F00", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "Hispanic Female", "#b3d4e8", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "Hispanic Male", "#56B4E9", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "Other Female", "#cca1b9", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "Other Male", "#CC79A7", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "White Female", "#a1a1a1", ifelse(ocme$race_sex == "White Male", "#000000", "yellow"))))))))

# grab the values i need from ocme
results <- select(ocme, Year, race_sex, per, color)
  
# add this to the chi squared df 
racesexmat <- rbind(racesexmat, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(racesexmat) <- cols

#racesexmat


# fill in missing years with NAs so they won't show up interpolated -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65097273/r-how-to-fill-up-missing-year-values-in-a-data-frame
#racesexmat <- racesexmat %>% complete(Year = 2009:2023)

stackedarea <- ggplot(data = racesexmat, aes(x=Year, y=Proportion, fill=Race_sex)) + 
    geom_area(aes(position = 'stack', group = Race_sex))+  scale_fill_manual(name = "Race/ethnicity and sex", values=rev(racesexmat$Color), labels = rev(racesexmat$Race_sex)) + ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for CT opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people")+theme_bw()+ scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = length(yearList))+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right")

print(stackedarea)

ggsave(plot=stackedarea, filename = paste0("images/rs_area_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)


```

### Significance testing for the number of alcohol-detected deaths

```{r chiSquaredEtoh, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

# get proportion of etoh for each year for younger people -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28195996/count-number-of-rows-matching-a-criteria
etohyoungcount <- c(sum(ocme_2009_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2010_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2011_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2012_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2013_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2014_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2015_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2016_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2017_young$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2018_young$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2019_young$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2020_young$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2021_young$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2022_young$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2023_young$EtOH ==1))

# get proportion for older people
etoholdcount <- c(sum(ocme_2009_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2010_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2011_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2012_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2013_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2014_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2015_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2016_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2017_old$et_oh == 1), sum(ocme_2018_old$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2019_old$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2020_old$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2021_old$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2022_old$EtOH == 1), sum(ocme_2023_old$EtOH ==1))

# combine vectors into df
etohcount <- data.frame(ocmeyearList, etohyoungcount, etoholdcount)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(etohcount) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# convert the "race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

etohchi <- etohcount[,-1]
rownames(etohchi) <- etohcount[,1]

as.matrix(etohchi)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795
  # I'm using Fisher's exact test if >20% of cell counts are <5, if not use chi squared
  # I get >20% <5 from https://www.ccjm.org/content/84/9_suppl_2/e20
  pvalue <- ifelse(sum(etohchi < 5)/(ncol(etohchi) * nrow(etohchi)) > 0.2, fisher.test(as.matrix(etohchi), workspace=2e6)$p.value, chisq.test(as.matrix(etohchi))$p.value)
  
  pvalue
```

```{r propXyl, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
xylold <- c(sum(ocme_2009_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2009_old), sum(ocme_2010_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2010_old), sum(ocme_2011_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2011_old), sum(ocme_2012_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2012_old), sum(ocme_2013_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2013_old), sum(ocme_2014_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2014_old), sum(ocme_2015_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2015_old), sum(ocme_2016_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2016_old), sum(ocme_2017_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2017_old), sum(ocme_2018_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2018_old), sum(ocme_2019_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2019_old), sum(ocme_2020_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2020_old), sum(ocme_2021_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2021_old), sum(ocme_2022_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2022_old), sum(ocme_2023_old$xylazine == 1)/nrow(ocme_2023_old))

# combine vectors into df
propxyl <- data.frame(ocmeyearList, xylyoung, xylold)

# change the col names to be more informative

# create grouped bar plot, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72449952/making-a-grouped-bar-chart-in-r
# getting the labels in the right position from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37587288/ggplot-label-bars-in-grouped-bar-plot
# info on changing legend title from here https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41649929/how-to-modify-a-legend-title-in-a-barplot-with-ggplot

# increasing line size from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14794599/how-to-change-line-width-in-ggplot
# line graph info from https://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-line-plot-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization


pxyllong  <- propxyl |>
  # Reshape data to long format
  pivot_longer(Younger:Older)

# create labels with the value of each proportion
pxyllong$labels <- round(pxyllong$value, 2)

pxyl <-  ggplot(data = pxyllong, aes(x = Year, y = value, fill = name, group=name, color=factor(name))) +
  # Implement a grouped bar chart
  # Implement a line graph
  geom_line(stat = "identity", size = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Proportion of xylazine in opioid-detected overdose deaths \n in CT by age group, 2009-2023") + ylab("Proportion") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + scale_fill_discrete(guide="none") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=propxyl$Year) + xlab("Year")+ coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) + guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Age group"))+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = labels, x = Year, y = value), nudge_x = 0.05, na.rm = FALSE, color = "black", size = 2.5, label.size = NA, fill = NA)

pxyl

ggsave(plot=pxyl, filename = "images/prop_xyl_all.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

### Significance testing for the number of xylazine-detected deaths

```{r chiSquaredXyl, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

# get proportion of xyl for each year for younger people -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28195996/count-number-of-rows-matching-a-criteria
xylyoungcount <- c(sum(ocme_2009_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2010_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2011_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2012_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2013_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2014_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2015_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2016_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2017_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2018_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2019_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2020_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2021_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2022_young$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2023_young$xylazine ==1))

# get proportion for older people
xyloldcount <- c(sum(ocme_2009_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2010_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2011_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2012_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2013_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2014_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2015_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2016_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2017_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2018_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2019_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2020_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2021_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2022_old$xylazine == 1), sum(ocme_2023_old$xylazine ==1))

# combine vectors into df
xylcount <- data.frame(ocmeyearList, xylyoungcount, xyloldcount)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(xylcount) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# convert the "race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

xylchi <- xylcount[,-1]
rownames(xylchi) <- xylcount[,1]

as.matrix(xylchi)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795
# getting rid of the nonzero entries for testing

  # I'm using Fisher's exact test if >20% of cell counts are <5, if not use chi squared
  # I get >20% <5 from https://www.ccjm.org/content/84/9_suppl_2/e20
  pvalue <- ifelse(sum(xylchi < 5)/(ncol(xylchi) * nrow(xylchi)) > 0.2, fisher.test(as.matrix(xylchi), workspace=2e6)$p.value, chisq.test(as.matrix(xylchi))$p.value)
  
  pvalue
```
